svg.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Six levers the screens pull: certainty against fear, the home-currency anchor, loaded wording, asking twice, the setting, borrowed trust.

g.text: 1 · Certainty against fear
"Fixed exchange rate guaranteed" against
"determined by your bank": a cost dressed up
as insurance against a risk that barely exists.
2 · The home-currency anchor
A Union Jack and a total in pounds feel
familiar; the euro option shows no total,
so there is nothing to compare.
3 · Loaded wording
"Without conversion" sounds like missing
a service; "with conversion" sounds like
the complete option.
4 · Asking twice
Two screens, the same choice: a second
chance to catch a tired traveller, and the
first answer framed as a mistake to fix.
5 · The setting
Standing at a machine in the street,
often with a queue behind: nobody does
the arithmetic there.
6 · Borrowed trust
It is a bank's machine, so "guaranteed"
reads as the bank looking after you.
The answer that pays: always the local currency.
